slot.brief: statement-based MCQ on symmetric/skew matrices: which of the given expressions (e.g. A+Aᵀ, AAᵀ, A−Aᵀ) is always symmetric or skew-symmetric

stem: If $A$ is any square matrix, then which of the following matrices is always symmetric?

verdicts.working: For (B), \((AA^T+A^TA)^T=AA^T+A^TA\), so it is always symmetric. The other options are not always symmetric.

working:
For any square matrix $A$, we have:
- $(A - A^T)^T = A^T - A = -(A - A^T)$, so it is skew-symmetric.
- $(A A^T)^T = A A^T$ and $(A^T A)^T = A^T A$, both are symmetric; the sum of symmetric matrices is symmetric, so $A A^T + A^T A$ is always symmetric.
- $A A^T A$ is not symmetric in general (e.g., $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ gives $A A^T A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$).
- $A^2 - A^T$ need not be symmetric (same $A$ gives $A^2 - A^T = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$).
Hence only option (B) is always symmetric.

Independent check: For (B), \((AA^T+A^TA)^T=AA^T+A^TA\), so it is always symmetric. The other options are not always symmetric.
solution:
Using $(XY)^T=Y^T X^T$, we get
$$
(AA^T+A^TA)^T=AA^T+A^TA.
$$
Hence $AA^T+A^TA$ is always symmetric, which is option (C).

draft.distractor_notes: Option A is skew-symmetric, a common confusion. Option C and D are chosen because students sometimes assume any product involving A and its transpose is symmetric, but products of three matrices need not be symmetric.
